reuse.why: Uses the existing db.first query helper and AccountSyncSource type; the tree has no shared link function to hook into, so a new guard is the natural reuse point.

duplication.why: The rule is written once in assertBankAccountNotLinked; the five link functions only repeat a short call with their provider and account id, which mirrors the already-duplicated link copies rather than adding new logic.

placement.why: The guard sits in server/accounts/app.ts beside the link handlers it protects, before any bank lookup or write; a db-layer query function would be marginally cleaner but nothing similar exists.

scope.why: Only adds the guard, its five call sites and focused tests.

maintainability.why: A single guard with the full 'what counts as linked' rule in one query is easy to own; a sixth provider must remember to call it because the link sequence itself is still copied per provider.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All five link handlers call the new guard; no existing abstraction is routed around.

disguised_duplication.where: No logic is duplicated; the per-provider additions are calls to one guard.

one_place.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked in server/accounts/app.ts holds the rule (same provider, same account id, not tombstoned, not the upgrading account) and is called by all five link handlers (goCardless, simpleFin, pluggyai, akahu, enableBanking).
